note: The codex registry: every day's key concepts, appended by the generator (and the council). rel[] edges draw the knowledge graph.

concepts.d: A tuple (S, A, P, R, γ) defining a sequential decision problem under uncertainty.
Model-free RL algorithm that learns the value of action-state pairs via temporal difference.
Updates value estimates based on the difference between successive predictions.
Directly optimizes a parameterized policy by computing gradients of expected return.
Monte-Carlo policy gradient algorithm using full episode returns as the signal.
Combines policy gradient (actor) with a value function baseline (critic) to reduce variance.
V(s): expected cumulative discounted reward from state s under a policy.
Tension between trying new actions (exploration) and using known good ones (exploitation).
With probability ε pick a random action; otherwise pick the greedy best action.
Allows a model to focus on relevant parts of the input when producing each output token.
Each token attends to all other tokens in the same sequence via Q, K, V projections.
Runs h parallel attention heads, each in a subspace, then concatenates and projects.
Encoder-decoder stack of self-attention and feed-forward layers; backbone of modern LLMs.
Adds order information to token embeddings since attention is permutation-invariant.
Splits raw text into sub-word units (BPE, WordPiece) that the model processes.
Iteratively merges the most frequent symbol pairs to build a fixed-size sub-word vocabulary.
The fixed set of tokens a model can emit; size trades coverage against embedding matrix cost.
A model that assigns probabilities to sequences, usually by predicting the next token.
Exponentiated average negative log-likelihood; lower is better for language models.
Continuing training a pretrained model on a task-specific dataset to specialise its weights.
Using representations learned on one task to accelerate learning on a related task.
A model trained on large general data, whose weights are reused as a starting point.
Low-Rank Adaptation: inserts small trainable rank-decomposition matrices, freezing base weights.
Techniques (LoRA, adapters, prefix-tuning) that fine-tune <1% of parameters.
Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback: trains a reward model on preferences, then RL-fine-tunes.
A classifier trained on human preference pairs to score outputs for RLHF.
Anthropic's method of self-critique and revision guided by a written set of principles.
Crafting input text to elicit desired model behaviour without changing weights.
Prompting the model to produce intermediate reasoning steps before the final answer.
Providing k labeled examples in the prompt so the model generalises to new instances.
Augments LLM generation with retrieved documents to ground answers in external knowledge.
Encodes queries and passages into vectors; retrieval is nearest-neighbour search.
A dense real-valued vector representation of a token, sentence or document.
Finding the k nearest vectors in a corpus, typically with cosine or dot-product distance.
HNSW, IVF, LSH — trade recall for speed when searching million-scale embedding corpora.
A cross-encoder that scores (query, passage) pairs to re-order a retrieved candidate set.
Splitting documents into passage-size units before embedding for retrieval.
The maximum number of tokens a model can attend to in a single forward pass.
When an LLM generates plausible-sounding but factually unsupported text.
Connecting model outputs to verifiable external sources to reduce hallucination.
LLM ability to call external functions or APIs and incorporate their results.
Structured API where the model emits JSON describing a function name and arguments.
Think → act → observe cycle where an LLM iterates tool calls until a goal is reached.
Interleaves Reasoning and Acting: the model writes a thought, an action, then observes.
Open standard for connecting AI models to external data and tools via a JSON-RPC transport.
Normalises layer inputs across the batch dimension during training to stabilise gradients.
Normalises across the feature dimension of each sample; preferred in Transformers.
During training, randomly zeros a fraction p of activations to prevent co-adaptation.
Techniques (L1, L2, dropout) that penalise complexity to reduce overfitting.
Chain-rule algorithm computing parameter gradients efficiently in deep networks.
Iteratively updates parameters in the direction of steepest loss decrease.
DAG representation of operations enabling automatic differentiation.
Adaptive moment estimation: combines momentum and RMSProp with bias correction.
Scalar controlling the step size during gradient descent; critical hyper-parameter.
Adjusts learning rate during training, e.g. cosine annealing or linear warm-up.
Sliding-window dot product that shares weights spatially; forms the core of CNNs.
Spatial downsampling operation (max or average) reducing feature map resolution.
Skip connection that adds a layer's input to its output, enabling very deep networks.
Architecture where encoder maps input to a latent representation, decoder generates output.
Generates output sequentially, conditioning each step on previously generated tokens.
Approximate decoding that keeps the top-k partial sequences at each step.
Scales logits before softmax; >1 flattens distribution, <1 sharpens it.
Nucleus sampling: samples from the smallest set of tokens whose probability sums to p.
Training a small student model to mimic a large teacher's soft output distribution.
Reducing weight precision (FP32→INT8/INT4) to shrink model size and speed inference.
Infrastructure for running model inference at scale: batching, caching, hardware selection.
Caches the key and value tensors from prior tokens to avoid recomputing attention.
IO-aware exact attention that tiles computation to stay in SRAM, dramatically reducing memory.
A small draft model proposes tokens; the large model verifies many in parallel.
Storing the KV cache of a reused prompt prefix to avoid recomputing it on each request.
Restricts each token to attend to a small subset of positions, reducing O(n²) cost.
Routes each token to a subset of specialised sub-networks, expanding capacity cheaply.
Replicates the model across devices; each device processes a different batch shard.
Splits individual weight matrices across devices so each holds a shard.
Distributes layers across devices; micro-batches flow through the pipeline.
Recomputes activations during backward pass, trading compute for memory.
Uses FP16/BF16 for forward/backward and FP32 for the master copy of weights.
Quantitative measures (BLEU, ROUGE, accuracy, F1, win-rate) for comparing model outputs.
A standardised evaluation dataset and scoring procedure for comparing models.
The practice of systematically measuring model capabilities and failure modes.
Adversarial testing by humans or models to surface harmful or undesired model behaviours.
Models that jointly process and generate multiple data types (text, images, audio, video).
Network (ViT, CLIP) that maps an image to a sequence of patch embeddings.
Contrastive Language-Image Pretraining: joint image-text embedding via contrastive loss.
Pulls similar pairs together and pushes dissimilar pairs apart in embedding space.
Generates data by learning to reverse a gradual Gaussian noise-addition process.
Learning the gradient of the data log-density, used as the backbone of diffusion.
Encodes inputs to a latent distribution and decodes samples; trained with ELBO.
Generator and discriminator trained adversarially; generator aims to fool the discriminator.
Training across decentralised devices without sharing raw data; gradients are aggregated.
Adds calibrated noise to gradients or outputs to bound information leakage about individuals.
Structured documentation of a model's intended use, limitations, and evaluation results.
Time to first token (TTFT) and time between tokens (TBT); critical UX metrics.
Tokens or requests processed per second; trades off with latency under batching.
BM25 and TF-IDF: lexical matching using inverted indexes; fast and interpretable.
Combines dense and sparse retrieval scores (via RRF or linear interpolation) for best recall.
Augmenting the query with related terms or generated hypothetical answers to improve recall.
Restricting retrieval to documents matching structured predicates (date, author, tag).
Chaining retrieval steps: the answer to one sub-query seeds the next retrieval.
Persistent store for chunks and their metadata, backing a retrieval system (Elasticsearch, pgvector).
Specialised store that indexes and queries high-dimensional embedding vectors (Pinecone, Weaviate).
Stores recent or frequent results to avoid redundant computation or retrieval.
Hard limit on how many tokens a request or generation may consume, for cost and safety.
Instructions prepended before the conversation that shape the model's behaviour and persona.
JSON Schema describing a function's name, parameters and types for LLM function-calling.
Component that plans high-level tasks and delegates subtasks to specialised agents or tools.
An agent spawned by an orchestrator to execute a bounded, well-defined subtask.
Component giving an agent persistent storage: episodic, semantic or working memory.
Explicit representation of agent states and transitions, adding predictability to complex flows.
Issuing multiple tool calls in one model turn to reduce round-trip latency.
Attack where malicious text in retrieved content overrides the system prompt's intent.
Adversarial prompts that bypass safety guardrails, eliciting restricted model behaviour.
Post-hoc classifier or guardrail layer that blocks harmful model outputs.
MoE with a top-k gating function activating only k of N experts per token.
Metrics like recall@k, MRR and nDCG measuring how well retrieved docs match ground truth.
Metrics for LLM output quality: faithfulness, answer relevance, coherence, fluency.
A well-calibrated model's stated confidence matches its empirical accuracy.
Training on examples ordered from easy to hard to improve sample efficiency.
Synthetically expanding training data via transformations to improve generalisation.
Model memorises training data and fails to generalise to unseen examples.
Model is too simple to capture the data's structure; both train and test error are high.
High bias → underfit; high variance → overfit. Optimal model balances both.
Standard classification loss: -Σ y log p̂; used for next-token prediction.
Sharing the embedding matrix between the input and output projection in LMs.
Encodes position via rotation matrices applied to Q and K; extrapolates to unseen lengths.
Shares K/V heads across groups of Q heads, reducing KV cache size with little quality loss.
Each token attends to only the w nearest tokens; O(n·w) instead of O(n²).
State-space model with selective state updates; linear inference cost vs quadratic attention.
Model adapts to a task from examples in the prompt without any weight updates.
Fine-tunes an LM on preference pairs without an explicit reward model, via a closed-form loss.
Odds Ratio Preference Optimisation: single-stage alignment without a reference model.
Fine-tuning on demonstration pairs (input, output) with cross-entropy loss.
SFT on (instruction, response) pairs to make models follow natural-language directives.
An LLM integrated with external tools (search, code interpreter, calculators) at inference.
Sandboxed execution environment that runs LLM-generated code and returns results.
Tool that queries a search engine and returns snippets for LLM grounding.
A URI-addressable data source (file, DB row, API endpoint) exposed by an MCP server.
A callable function exposed by an MCP server, schema-described, invoked by the model.
MCP server requests that the client LLM generate text; inverts control for agentic workflows.
Interleaving chain-of-thought reasoning steps with tool calls in a single agent turn.
Breaking a complex task into subtasks an agent or orchestrator can tackle sequentially.
Agent first generates a full plan, then executes steps, re-planning when blocked.
Model decision of which tool to call given context; quality depends on prompt and schema clarity.
Each agent step receives an observation (tool result) and emits the next action.
Sending generated tokens to the client as they are produced, reducing perceived latency.
Continuous or dynamic batching groups requests to maximise GPU utilisation.
Multiple requests with the same system prompt share one KV cache copy.
Directing easy queries to small cheap models and hard ones to larger expensive models.
Maximum allowable end-to-end time for a request, allocated across retrieval, inference, postprocessing.
Throttling API requests per token or per time window to manage cost and abuse.
Fraction of time a system is operational and serving requests correctly.
Ability of a system to continue operating correctly when components fail.
Maintaining copies of data or services on multiple nodes to increase availability and durability.
All nodes see the same data at the same time (strong), or eventually converge (eventual).
A distributed system can guarantee at most two of Consistency, Availability, Partition Tolerance.
Horizontally partitioning data across nodes so each holds a subset.
Maps keys and nodes onto a ring so only k/n keys remap when a node joins or leaves.
Distributes incoming requests across backend instances; layer-4 (TCP) or layer-7 (HTTP).
Geographically distributed caches that serve static assets close to the user.
Durable buffer decoupling producers from consumers; Kafka, SQS, RabbitMQ.
Components communicate by producing and consuming events, loosely coupled.
Signal propagated upstream when a consumer is overwhelmed, slowing producers.
Stops requests to a failing service after a threshold and retries after a cool-down.
Token bucket or leaky bucket algorithm to cap request rates per client.
Single entry point for microservices: routing, auth, rate limiting, logging.
Infra layer (Istio, Linkerd) handling service-to-service communication, telemetry, auth.
An operation that can be retried safely: applying it multiple times yields the same result.
Distributed protocol ensuring all participants commit or all abort a transaction.
Chains local transactions with compensating transactions on failure, avoiding 2PC.
Command Query Responsibility Segregation: separate models for reads and writes.
Persisting state as an immutable log of events; current state is derived by replaying.
Durably logs changes before applying them, enabling crash recovery and replication.
Space-efficient probabilistic set membership: false positives possible, false negatives not.
Self-balancing tree with high branching factor; underpins most relational DB indexes.
Log-Structured Merge Tree: writes go to an in-memory buffer, flushed as immutable SSTables.
Stores each column contiguously on disk; excellent for analytical scans, poor for point writes.
Online Analytical Processing (aggregations, wide scans) vs Online Transactional Processing (point reads/writes).
Data and compute replicated across geographic regions for latency and disaster recovery.
Flat-namespace key-value store for large blobs (S3, GCS); high throughput, eventual consistency.
Optimised for append-mostly timestamped data: InfluxDB, TimescaleDB, Prometheus.
Stores entities as nodes and relationships as edges; efficient traversal (Neo4j, Neptune).
Inverted index mapping terms to document lists, the core of Elasticsearch and Solr.
Policy for removing items when cache is full: LRU, LFU, FIFO, ARC.
Mechanism to expire stale cached content: TTL, event-based purge, surrogate keys.
Central store for message schemas (Avro/Protobuf) enabling producer-consumer compatibility.
Processing events as they arrive with low latency: Kafka Streams, Flink, Spark Streaming.
Processing large volumes of data at scheduled intervals: Spark, Hadoop MapReduce.
Combines batch and stream layers: batch for accuracy, speed layer for freshness.
Service that maps a short key to a long URL via a redirect, with high read:write ratio.
Distributed rate limiter using Redis INCR with TTL or token-bucket in a central store.
Fan-out service routing alerts to push, email, SMS channels via async queues.
Fan-out-on-write (celebrity: fan-out-on-read) delivering posts to follower timelines.
Returns top-k completions for a prefix in <100 ms using trie or inverted index + cache.
Distributed system fetching and indexing web pages: frontier queue, DNS cache, dedup bloom filter.
Requires exactly-once semantics, idempotency keys, reconciliation and ledger append-only writes.
Concurrency challenge: prevent double-booking via distributed locks or optimistic concurrency.
Encode at multiple bitrates, store in object storage, serve via CDN, adapt via HLS/DASH.
RTMP ingest → WebRTC or HLS with 2–5 s latency; transcoding at edge for multi-bitrate.
Collects, aggregates and stores time-series metrics: Prometheus scrape → remote_write → Thanos.
Mutual exclusion across nodes: Redlock (Redis), ZooKeeper, etcd; each with trade-offs.
Single node acts as coordinator; Raft or ZooKeeper ZAB ensure consensus on leader identity.
Nodes propagate state to random peers; eventually consistent, robust to failures.
W + R > N ensures that at least one node has the latest write; trades availability for consistency.
Logical timestamps that capture causal ordering between events in a distributed system.
Workers pull jobs from a queue (Celery, BullMQ) for async background processing.
Framework (Temporal, Durable Functions) that persists workflow state so crashes are transparent.
Intentionally injecting failures to verify system resilience and fault-tolerance.
Service-Level Objective (internal target) and Service-Level Agreement (contractual promise).
Applies software engineering to operations: error budgets, toil reduction, blameless post-mortems.
Client and server exchange supported feature sets at initialization so both sides adapt gracefully.
מערכת שמציגה חברים גיאוגרפיים בזמן אמת. מבוססת geohash לחיפוש שכנות, Redis GEOADD לאחסון, Kafka ל-event streaming ו-WebSocket לדחיפה.
Redis Sorted Set שמקודד קואורדינטות כ-geohash. GEOADD מוסיף נקודה, GEOSEARCH מחזיר כל מה שבתוך radius. O(log n) על N משתמשים.
שירות שמקבל עדכוני GPS ממכשירים, מחשב geohash, מעדכן Redis ו-Cassandra, ומפרסם events ל-Kafka. TTL קצר ב-Redis כדי שמשתמשים לא פעילים לא יופיעו בתוצאות.
